requirements.requirement: Kernel parameter audit=1 is configured to be applied on boot (via grubby/BLS and /etc/default/grub) on node1
requirements.summary: grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="audit=1" succeeded (return code 0). Verification showed the BLS entry (/boot/loader/entries/...conf), grubby --info=ALL output, and /etc/default/grub GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX all now include audit=1, ensuring the setting applies to all installed kernels and future kernel installs.

requirements.requirement: Setting persists and takes effect across an actual reboot (not just configuration)
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-restart boot_id (4cee4ea8-...) was captured, a reboot was issued and acknowledged, connectivity was lost during the transition (timeouts/connection reset), and a new, different boot_id (7e2dad6f-...) was observed afterward, proving a genuine restart. Post-reboot /proc/cmdline contains audit=1 and dmesg shows 'audit: enabled (after initialization)', directly demonstrating the parameter is live in the newly booted kernel.

requirements.requirement: Node remained otherwise healthy (no service damage, no package inconsistency) through the change and reboot
requirements.summary: Lifecycle snapshots show no failed systemd units and identical package-manager health before and after; listening sockets (ssh, chrony, port 9090) are present in both snapshots with only PID changes expected from a reboot.

overall_summary: The executor configured audit=1 persistently via grubby across BLS entries and /etc/default/grub, then performed an actual reboot of node1, capturing a pre-restart healthy baseline boot_id, an acknowledged restart, a differing post-restart boot_id, and direct confirmation that /proc/cmdline and dmesg show audit=1 active in the new boot. This is a complete before/during/after evidence chain for a persistence-related requirement, satisfying the task contract. The only hygiene issue is a small leftover /tmp/reboot.log file from the backgrounded reboot command, which is low-risk and does not affect functionality.
limitations: Persistence was only demonstrated across a single reboot cycle; a second reboot was not performed, though the configuration mechanism (grubby --update-kernel=ALL plus BLS/grub defaults) supports durability beyond one cycle.
auditd service status (systemctl is-active auditd => inactive) was observed but is outside the scope of the stated task, which concerns only the kernel boot parameter, not the userspace audit daemon.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were almost entirely read-only discovery/verification plus the single necessary grubby mutation and the necessary reboot. One minor unnecessary residue: the backgrounded reboot command (cmd-c5b2c6558804420a) redirected output to /tmp/reboot.log, which was never cleaned up and appears as an added file in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot. This is bounded, low-risk, non-sensitive residue (just reboot command stdout/stderr) with no security or functional impact, but it was left behind rather than removed after its diagnostic purpose was served.
